title: Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) — San Miguel County — 333 W Colorado Ave - San Miguel County
summary: The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) serves to ensure the health of income-eligible pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding women, infants, and children under 5 years of age by providing:   An eWIC debit card to purchase free, healthy foods  Personalized nutrition information  Referrals to community services  Breastfeeding support, including:  Breast pumps and supplies  Lactation experts and breastfeeding peer counselors  Support groups  Classes

fields.location name: 333 W Colorado Ave - San Miguel County
fields.physical address: 333 W Colorado Ave, 3rd Fl, Telluride, CO, 81435
fields.service summary: The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) serves to ensure the health of income-eligible pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding women, infants, and children under 5 years of age by providing:   An eWIC debit card to purchase free, healthy foods  Personalized nutrition information  Referrals to community services  Breastfeeding support, including:  Breast pumps and supplies  Lactation experts and breastfeeding peer counselors  Support groups  Classes
fields.eligibility: Individuals must:   Live in Colorado  Be 1 of the following:  Currently pregnant  Breastfeeding a baby less than 12 months old  Pregnant within the past 6 months  Aged under 5 and under  The father, grandparent, foster parent, or guardian of a child under 5 years of age    Meet income guidelines (as defined below)   If a household member is receiving Medicaid, TANF, SNAP or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), individuals may be automatically income-eligible for WIC. If no one in the household participates in any of these programs, the household’s gross income (before taxes), must be at or below the amounts listed below. If the household income is slightly above the guidelines, contact a WIC clinic to discuss potential eligibility. Income Eligibility Requirements (July 1st, 2026 - June 30th, 2027)  Household Size - Gross Monthly Income Limits  1 - $2,461  2 - $3,337  3 - $4,212  4 - $5,088  5 - $5,964  6 - $6,839  7 - $7,715  8 - $8,591   Each Additional Person: Add $876  Individuals who are pregnant may count as a 2 person household. Area Served: San Miguel County
fields.access method: Visit the following link to schedule an appointment with the nearest clinic: coloradowic.gov/find-wic-clinic. Clients may also visit the following link to request a call from a WIC clinic: coloradowicsignup.com. A WIC staff member will contact the client within 10 days to see if they qualify and help set up an appointment.
fields.required documents: Must provide:    Identification for all family members applying for WIC   Proof of address   Proof of participation in Medicaid, SNAP, TANF, or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), or proof of income (e.g. paystub, tax return, letter from employer)  Growth measurements (height and weight) taken within the last 60 days and hemoglobin levels, if applicable
fields.hours of operation: Monday - Friday, 9 a.m. - 5 p.m. (Administrative Hours); Hours Vary (WIC Clinic)

fields.organization name: Sedgwick County Department of Human Services
fields.service summary: The Low-Income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP) is a federally funded program that helps eligible Colorado households with a portion of their winter home heating costs. Applications are accepted each year from November 1st - April 30th. The benefit does not cover the full cost of heating and is offered once per season. LEAP payments are made directly to the household’s primary heating fuel vendor or utility. Household types may include those using fuels such as:   Wood   Coal   Propane   Heat billed on a shared meter
fields.eligibility: Applicants must:    Be a permanent legal resident of the United States and Colorado, or have a household member that is a US citizen   Pay home heating costs to a heating provider, fuel dealer, or landlord as part of rent   Have a maximum household income that falls within the guidelines below    'Household” means people who live with you and for whom you are financially responsible. title: Low-Income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP) — Summit County Department of Human Services — 360 Peak One Dr - Summit County
summary: The Low-Income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP) is a federally funded program that helps eligible Colorado households with a portion of their winter home heating costs. Applications are accepted each year from November 1st - April 30th. The benefit does not cover the full cost of heating and is offered once per season. LEAP payments are made directly to the household’s primary heating fuel vendor or utility. Household types may include those using fuels such as:   Wood   Coal   Propane   Heat billed on a shared meter

fields.physical address: 360 Peak One Dr, Ste 230, Frisco, CO, 80443
fields.service summary: The Low-Income Energy Assistance Program (LEAP) is a federally funded program that helps eligible Colorado households with a portion of their winter home heating costs. Applications are accepted each year from November 1st - April 30th. The benefit does not cover the full cost of heating and is offered once per season. LEAP payments are made directly to the household’s primary heating fuel vendor or utility. Household types may include those using fuels such as:   Wood   Coal   Propane   Heat billed on a shared meter
fields.eligibility: Applicants must:    Be a permanent legal resident of the United States and Colorado, or have a household member that is a US citizen   Pay home heating costs to a heating provider, fuel dealer, or landlord as part of rent   Have a maximum household income that falls within the guidelines below    'Household” means people who live with you and for whom you are financially responsible. Household Size Monthly Gross    Income for the 2025-2026 Season                 60% of State Median Income    1 - $3,607  2 - $4,717  3 - $5,827  4 - $6,938  5 - $8,048  6 - $9,158  7 - $9,366  8 - $9,574  Each Additional Person $208    Area Served: Summit County
fields.access method: Apply online. Visit the website to download a paper application and drop off at the local DHS office or mail/email to the county to process. Call to request a mailed paper application, to apply over the phone, or for more information.
fields.required documents: Must provide:    Proof of citizenship if born outside of the US   Proof of all monthly household income    If self-employed, receipts for all expenses claimed on profit and loss statement   Copy of most recent heating bill or recent rent receipt, if heat is included with rent
fields.hours of operation: November 1st - April 30th (Application Open); Monday - Friday, 8 a.m. - 5 p.m. (Administrative Hours)

fields.physical address: 360 Peak One Dr, Ste 230, Frisco, CO, 80443
fields.service summary: The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) serves to ensure the health of income-eligible pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding women, infants, and children under 5 years of age by providing:   An eWIC debit card to purchase free, healthy foods  Personalized nutrition information  Referrals to community services  Breastfeeding support, including:  Breast pumps and supplies  Lactation experts and breastfeeding peer counselors  Support groups  Classes
fields.eligibility: Individuals must:   Live in Colorado  Be 1 of the following:  Currently pregnant  Breastfeeding a baby less than 12 months old  Pregnant within the past 6 months  Aged under 5 and under  The father, grandparent, foster parent, or guardian of a child under 5 years of age    Meet income guidelines (as defined below)   If a household member is receiving Medicaid, TANF, SNAP or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), individuals may be automatically income-eligible for WIC. If no one in the household participates in any of these programs, the household’s gross income (before taxes), must be at or below the amounts listed below. If the household income is slightly above the guidelines, contact a WIC clinic to discuss potential eligibility. Income Eligibility Requirements (July 1st, 2026 - June 30th, 2027)  Household Size - Gross Monthly Income Limits  1 - $2,461  2 - $3,337  3 - $4,212  4 - $5,088  5 - $5,964  6 - $6,839  7 - $7,715  8 - $8,591   Each Additional Person: Add $876  Individuals who are pregnant may count as a 2 person household. Area Served: Summit County
fields.access method: Visit the following link to schedule an appointment with the nearest clinic: coloradowic.gov/find-wic-clinic. Clients may also visit the following link to request a call from a WIC clinic: coloradowicsignup.com. A WIC staff member will contact the client within 10 days to see if they qualify and help set up an appointment.
fields.required documents: Must provide:    Identification for all family members applying for WIC   Proof of address   Proof of participation in Medicaid, SNAP, TANF, or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), or proof of income (e.g. paystub, tax return, letter from employer)  Growth measurements (height and weight) taken within the last 60 days and hemoglobin levels, if applicable

title: Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) — Sunrise Community Health — 4209 County Rd 24 1/2 - Weld County
summary: The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) serves to ensure the health of income-eligible pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding women, infants, and children under 5 years of age by providing:   An eWIC debit card to purchase free, healthy foods  Personalized nutrition information  Referrals to community services  Breastfeeding support, including:  Breast pumps and supplies  Lactation experts and breastfeeding peer counselors  Support groups  Classes

fields.service summary: The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) serves to ensure the health of income-eligible pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding women, infants, and children under 5 years of age by providing:   An eWIC debit card to purchase free, healthy foods  Personalized nutrition information  Referrals to community services  Breastfeeding support, including:  Breast pumps and supplies  Lactation experts and breastfeeding peer counselors  Support groups  Classes
fields.eligibility: Individuals must:   Live in Colorado  Be 1 of the following:  Currently pregnant  Breastfeeding a baby less than 12 months old  Pregnant within the past 6 months  Aged under 5 and under  The father, grandparent, foster parent, or guardian of a child under 5 years of age    Meet income guidelines (as defined below)   If a household member is receiving Medicaid, TANF, SNAP or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), individuals may be automatically income-eligible for WIC. If no one in the household participates in any of these programs, the household’s gross income (before taxes), must be at or below the amounts listed below. If the household income is slightly above the guidelines, contact a WIC clinic to discuss potential eligibility. Income Eligibility Requirements (July 1st, 2026 - June 30th, 2027)  Household Size - Gross Monthly Income Limits  1 - $2,461  2 - $3,337  3 - $4,212  4 - $5,088  5 - $5,964  6 - $6,839  7 - $7,715  8 - $8,591   Each Additional Person: Add $876  Individuals who are pregnant may count as a 2 person household. Area Served: Statewide
fields.access method: Visit the following link to schedule an appointment with the nearest clinic: coloradowic.gov/find-wic-clinic. Clients may also visit the following link to request a call from a WIC clinic: coloradowicsignup.com. A WIC staff member will contact the client within 10 days to see if they qualify and help set up an appointment.
fields.required documents: Must provide:    Identification for all family members applying for WIC   Proof of address   Proof of participation in Medicaid, SNAP, TANF, or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), or proof of income (e.g. paystub, tax return, letter from employer)  Growth measurements (height and weight) taken within the last 60 days and hemoglobin levels, if applicable
fields.hours of operation: Monday - Friday, 8 a.m. - 5 p.m. (Administrative Hours); Hours Vary (WIC Hours)

title: Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) — Teller County Department of Public Health — 11115 W Hwy 24 - Teller County
summary: The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) serves to ensure the health of income-eligible pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding women, infants, and children under 5 years of age by providing:   An eWIC debit card to purchase free, healthy foods  Personalized nutrition information  Referrals to community services  Breastfeeding support, including:  Breast pumps and supplies  Lactation experts and breastfeeding peer counselors  Support groups  Classes

fields.organization name: Teller County Department of Public Health
fields.service summary: The Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) serves to ensure the health of income-eligible pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding women, infants, and children under 5 years of age by providing:   An eWIC debit card to purchase free, healthy foods  Personalized nutrition information  Referrals to community services  Breastfeeding support, including:  Breast pumps and supplies  Lactation experts and breastfeeding peer counselors  Support groups  Classes
fields.eligibility: Individuals must:   Live in Colorado  Be 1 of the following:  Currently pregnant  Breastfeeding a baby less than 12 months old  Pregnant within the past 6 months  Aged under 5 and under  The father, grandparent, foster parent, or guardian of a child under 5 years of age    Meet income guidelines (as defined below)   If a household member is receiving Medicaid, TANF, SNAP or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), individuals may be automatically income-eligible for WIC. If no one in the household participates in any of these programs, the household’s gross income (before taxes), must be at or below the amounts listed below. If the household income is slightly above the guidelines, contact a WIC clinic to discuss potential eligibility. Income Eligibility Requirements (July 1st, 2026 - June 30th, 2027)  Household Size - Gross Monthly Income Limits  1 - $2,461  2 - $3,337  3 - $4,212  4 - $5,088  5 - $5,964  6 - $6,839  7 - $7,715  8 - $8,591   Each Additional Person: Add $876  Individuals who are pregnant may count as a 2 person household. Area Served: Teller County
fields.access method: Visit the following link to schedule an appointment with the nearest clinic: coloradowic.gov/find-wic-clinic. Clients may also visit the following link to request a call from a WIC clinic: coloradowicsignup.com. A WIC staff member will contact the client within 10 days to see if they qualify and help set up an appointment.
fields.required documents: Must provide:    Identification for all family members applying for WIC   Proof of address   Proof of participation in Medicaid, SNAP, TANF, or FDPIR (Food Distribution Program on Indian Reservations), or proof of income (e.g. paystub, tax return, letter from employer)  Growth measurements (height and weight) taken within the last 60 days and hemoglobin levels, if applicable
